mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk was most worthwhile: it showed that muscles need both nerve signals and materials carried by blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the digestive and urinary organs was clear, but mostly felt like filling named spaces rather than making a difficult decision.

surprise.text: The diaphragm separates the chest and abdomen, yet nerves, blood vessels and the food pipe cross between them by their own routes. That helped me picture the connection.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though several pairings followed named slots or goals rather than requiring much deduction.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter explored how the assembled systems work together. This chapter was a satisfying recap, though many placements were predictable.
